messages:
AcmeNetOps: Hey team — since yesterday our on‑prem service behind the site‑to‑site VPN started failing calls to Redwood. Intermittent 401s and sometimes TLS errors. Nothing changed on our app side. Can you help triage?

alex: Sorry you hit this. Can you paste a short repro (curl) and any TLS/curl output? Also are you going through a corporate proxy or DPI box?

AcmeNetOps: Yes we route outbound through a transparent TLS‑inspecting proxy and we also have split‑horizon DNS for internal hosts. Quick curl output:

```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>"
* Connected to proxy.mycorp.internal (10.0.0.5) port 3128 (#0)
* TLSv1.2 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* SSL peer handshake failed, SSL error: certificate verify failed
* Closing connection 0
curl: (60) SSL: certificate verification failed
```

Sometimes it times out instead: `curl: (7) Failed to connect to api.redwood.ai port 443: Connection timed out`

maria: Two likely issues given your setup: (1) split DNS returning internal or NXDOMAIN for api.redwood.ai, (2) TLS MITM/proxy rewriting certs and possibly stripping SNI which breaks virtual‑hosted TLS endpoints. Can you run these quick checks?

1) `nslookup api.redwood.ai` from the host that runs the client
2) `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -showcerts`
3) `traceroute -n auth.redwood.ai` (auth calls are what validate tokens)

AcmeNetOps: Ran them. nslookup returns `10.100.200.15` (internal resolver answer). openssl output:

```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=1 C = US, O = "Corp Proxy CA" ...
verify error:num=19:self signed certificate in certificate chain
subject=/CN=10.0.0.5
issuer=/CN=Corp Proxy CA
---
No peer certificate available
---
```

traceroute shows it stops at our proxy (10.0.0.5) and doesn't go out to the public internet (we use NAT on the proxy).

infra-bot: Note: observed spikes in failed egress to api.redwood.ai from that CIDR during 2026‑03‑16 22:00–22:30 UTC.

priya: That confirms two things: your DNS is answering internal IPs (split‑horizon) and your proxy performs TLS interception presenting an internal cert. Redwood endpoints rely on SNI for routing to the right certificate and also for hosted auth flows. If the proxy is replacing certs and/or removing SNI, token validation and host verification will fail and lead to 401/SSL errors.

sean: Quick repro you can try to isolate: set NO_PROXY / bypass the proxy for redwood domains and see if calls succeed. On a test host: `export NO_PROXY=api.redwood.ai,auth.redwood.ai` then retry the curl. If you can't route direct due to security, ask network to allow TLS passthrough for those FQDNs (SNI passthrough) or to whitelist Redwood egress IP ranges.

AcmeNetOps: We tried NO_PROXY on the app host — same result, traceroute still hits 10.0.0.5 (VPN forces all egress via proxy). We also saw the auth call failing with a JSON body: `{"error":"token_validation_failed","message":"could not reach auth.redwood.ai"}` which aligns with traceroute.

maria: Two possible fixes (short term vs long term):
- Short term: Network to add explicit allowlist for outbound to Redwood hosts (api.redwood.ai, auth.redwood.ai) with TLS passthrough (no MITM) or route to an egress IP range that avoids the proxy. This preserves certificate chain and SNI.
- Long term: Update split‑horizon DNS so internal resolvers return public addresses for Redwood (or ensure proxy resolves and forwards the right SNI).

priya: For support debugging we need: 1) a packet capture of TLS ClientHello from a failing client (to confirm SNI field), 2) output of `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -cipher 'ALL' -msg` from the host if possible, 3) whether your proxy injects a corporate root into clients (it looks like it does).

AcmeNetOps: I'll coordinate with NetOps. One wrinkle: corporate policy requires TLS inspection for all outbound by default. Is there a recommended allowlist we can give them so it is minimal?

alex: We can provide a minimal set: whitelist FQDNs `api.redwood.ai`, `auth.redwood.ai`, `embeddings.redwood.ai`, and our control plane domains. Also allow outbound to these hostnames on 443 with TLS passthrough. If NetOps needs IPs for firewall rules we can share our egress IP ranges — I'll escalate to infra to provide the current ranges (we'll send them in the private support ticket, don't post IP ranges in public threads).

sean: If NetOps insists on MITM for auditing, you can still make it work by installing the corporate CA into the host trust store so `curl` and the app accept the proxy cert, but note this will hide our real cert chain and can break auth if the proxy removes SNI or rewrites host headers. So TLS passthrough is preferred for these endpoints.

AcmeNetOps: Understood. We'll open a change ticket to allow TLS passthrough for the three FQDNs and test with NO_PROXY after change.

maria: Also, for quick verification after NetOps change, try: `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:34.120.12.34 https://api.redwood.ai/health` (replace with a public egress IP) — that will confirm cert/SNI path if DNS is still sticky.

AcmeNetOps: Thanks all — we'll schedule a debug window tomorrow 15:00 UTC and I'll attach tcpdump/openssl output before the call. :thumbsup:
